hook_text: The soil under your feet used to be solid rock. So how did it get so soft?
clip_script: Harrismith, Free State. A road cut through a hill, like a slice of cake. Top: dark topsoil, full of roots. Middle: paler subsoil with stones. Bottom: solid rock. How did rock become soil? Sun heats it, night cools it, ice wedges it, roots split it, rivers roll it, wind scrapes it. Weathering! Add earthworms and rotting leaves for humus. Wait hundreds of years. Topsoil!
visual_style: Whiteboard road cutting showing topsoil, subsoil and rock, with arrows from cracking rock to tiny grains.
mood: Curious and patient, with a sense of deep time.
pacing: One big slice of earth, a fast list of rock breakers, then a slow, slow build-up of soil.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and look for soil layers next time you pass a road cutting.
